title: How early should you arrive at Cork Airport?
author: Brogan
cover_image_alt: Green and white Aer Lingus planes parked at the gates of an Irish airport under a cloudy sky
intro: Cork Airport asks you to arrive at least 90 minutes before a scheduled flight and 2½ hours before a charter. Here's how to plan your timing, with the 100ml liquids rule, the airport buses and the busy days.
seo_description: At least 90 minutes before a scheduled flight and 2½ hours before a charter, says Cork Airport. Liquids, busy days and the 225 and 226 buses.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Scheduled flights:** at least 90 minutes
- **Charter and package flights:** 2½ hours
- **Bank holiday weekends:** add 30 minutes
- **Liquids:** still 100ml

This is Cork Airport's own advice, checked in November 2026. Your airline's bag drop and gate deadlines are the ones that count, and they're on your booking. Procedures change, so check the airport's and the airline's current advice before you travel.

sections.heading: Why Cork is usually quick
sections.text:
Cork is the Republic of Ireland's second-busiest airport, but it has a single terminal, and the walk from the door to security to the gates is short. On most days, the 90-minute advice leaves plenty of time.

The exception is the busy waves. Many flights leave in the early morning, and the airport is at its busiest over bank holiday weekends, around Christmas and in the summer holidays. Over the St Brigid's bank holiday weekend in February 2026, the airport expected around 34,000 passengers, so a little extra time on those days is sensible. Charter and package holiday flights, such as sun and ski charters, often have bigger groups checking bags at the same time, which is why the airport asks for 2½ hours.

sections.heading: How early for your flight
sections.text:
| Trip | Flight | Arrive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| City break, hand luggage only | Midweek, mid-morning | **About 90 minutes** before |
| Scheduled flight, bags to drop | Friday evening | **About 2 hours** before |
| Package holiday charter | Any time | **2½ hours** before |
| Bank holiday or Christmas trip | Early morning | **2 to 2½ hours** before |

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.text:
Cork still uses the 100ml rule. Liquids, gels and pastes must be in containers of 100ml or less, in a clear, resealable bag, and you take the bag out at security. Cork Airport doesn't hand out plastic bags, but you can buy them in the terminal before security.

That's due to change. The airport is building a new security area with new scanners, which it expects to finish around Christmas 2026. Once it opens, you shouldn't need to take out liquids or laptops, as already happens in Dublin.

Watch out: until Cork's new security area is open, pack to 100ml even if you've flown from Dublin with bigger bottles. Check the airport's website for the switch-over date before you pack.

sections.heading: Bag drop and the gate
sections.image_alt: Silhouettes of passengers walking to a plane past the windows of an airport gate
sections.image_caption: The gate usually closes before the departure time on your ticket, so don't wait for the last call.
sections.text:
If you're checking a bag, plan around the bag drop deadline, not the departure time. Airlines close bag drop and check-in at set times before departure, often 40 to 60 minutes, and they don't make exceptions.

Ryanair has changed its bag drop times across its European airports, so if you're flying Ryanair from Cork, check the times in the app or on your booking rather than going by what you did last time.

Tip: check in online as soon as it opens. With hand luggage only and your boarding pass on your phone, you can go straight to security.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text:
- **By bus:** Bus Éireann routes **225** and **226** run between Cork city centre and the airport, stopping at Parnell Place bus station and Kent railway station. They run about every 30 minutes from Monday to Saturday and hourly on Sundays and bank holidays. The journey from Parnell Place takes about 25 minutes.
- **By train and bus:** Irish Rail lets you add the bus from Kent station to the airport when you book a train ticket, handy if you're coming from Dublin, Limerick or further afield.
- **By car:** the airport is about 6 km south of the city. Book parking ahead online for the best price.
- **Drop-off:** there's a set-down area outside the terminal. Check the airport's website for the current time limits and charges before you travel.

Allow extra time on the roads around the city at rush hour.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Cork?
sections.text:
Cork's routes have included sun spots like [Málaga](/destinations/malaga), [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) and [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote), and city breaks to [Prague](/destinations/prague), [Rome](/destinations/rome), [Barcelona](/destinations/barcelona), [Seville](/destinations/seville) and [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam). Routes change each season, so check the airport's destinations page for what's flying on your dates.

For more ideas, browse the [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page. If your family can't agree, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put everyone's picks into a draw.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Cork Airport?
faqs.answer: Cork Airport advises at least 90 minutes before a scheduled flight and at least 2½ hours before a charter flight. Allow more on bank holiday weekends and around Christmas.

faqs.question: Can you take more than 100ml of liquid through Cork Airport?
faqs.answer: Not yet. Cork still uses the 100ml rule, with liquids in a clear bag. A new security area with new scanners is expected around Christmas 2026.

faqs.question: Is there a bus from Cork city to Cork Airport?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bus Éireann routes 225 and 226 run from Parnell Place and Kent station, about every 30 minutes from Monday to Saturday and hourly on Sundays. The journey takes about 25 minutes.

faqs.question: How many terminals does Cork Airport have?
faqs.answer: One. All flights use the same terminal.
